en: Although some consider Andres Bonifacio the first president, Emilio Aguinaldo is officially recognized as the first Philippine president.
Contrary to popular belief, the sampaguita is not native to the Philippines but was introduced from China.
Although many still associate it with July 4, Philippine independence was officially proclaimed on June 12, 1898.
Although often mistaken for a single tribe, Igorot is an umbrella term for several Cordilleran ethnolinguistic groups.
While often thought to be pure Tagalog, the Filipino language actively incorporates words from other native Philippine languages.
Although often depicted facing his executioners, Jose Rizal actually turned his back to the firing squad at Bagumbayan.
Although Jose Rizal is the most prominent, the Philippines actually has no officially declared sole national hero.
Although often described as a cession, Spain actually sold the Philippines to the United States for twenty million dollars.
Contrary to fears of absolute power, the Constitution limits the President's martial law declaration to sixty days.
While some mistakenly credit her with inventing the incubator, Fe del Mundo actually designed an improvised bamboo one.
Although featuring indigenous Ati elements, Ati-Atihan is not a purely pagan ritual but a Catholic festival honoring Santo Niño.
Despite the myth of discovery, Ferdinand Magellan did not discover the Philippines, as thriving indigenous communities already existed.
